newsitem.title: CHILE: Banco Santiago mulls $150 mln capital increase.
newsitem.headline: Banco Santiago mulls $150 mln capital increase.

text.p: Recently merged Banco Santiago is studying a $150 million capital increase to meet requirements in Chile's new banking law, reported newspaper El Mercurio on Friday.

"Under the new law we will be under the Basil 10 standard and obviously we believe that being the country's largest bank we must have the necessary capital to carry out all the business we wish," said newly appointed president Andronico Luksic.
Bank stockholders approved an unspecified capital increase at a meeting Thursday.
Shareholders also voted that the bank's dividend payout ratio should not exceed 70 percent of net income this year. The remaining profits will be capitalized.
Banco Santiago was created in January from the merger of Banco O'Higgins and Banco de Santiago.
